first_impression.reaction: I Googled 'greece wedding packages' because every resort PDF I've opened says 'package' and means something different. The first line says exactly that: 'Two package documents from two Greek resorts can share a title and describe quite different weddings.' No 'say I do in paradise', just the actual problem. Then it tells me where they differ: rooms, exclusive use, transfers, suppliers. That's my list of worries. Kept reading.

journey.quote: Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before paying any deposit.
journey.reaction: That's lawyer advice, not wedding-blog advice. Currency is in there, which is the thing that keeps me up at night. Good start.

journey.quote: The same package lists the bouquet and boutonniere, a decorated club car, sparkling wine and Greek wedding sweets after the ceremony, taped music, a wedding cake and a room for the groom to prepare in from 14.00.
journey.reaction: Useful to see what's actually on the page, but 'taped music' and a 'decorated club car' is exactly the resort-package feel we're trying to avoid. Not the article's fault, but it confirms my suspicion that a venue package alone won't feel like us.

journey.quote: Each includes a choice of beach or poolside venue, lanterns, petals and a floral table display, sparkling wine and cake after the ceremony and photographs from the hotel photographer, scaled to up to 10, 20 or 30 guests by option.
journey.reaction: Up to 30 guests. We're 60 to 90, so Euphoria's off the list in one sentence. I like that the numbers are there so I can rule things out fast.

journey.quote: Not published: whether the government fees Melenos attends to sit inside or outside its costing.
journey.reaction: Telling me what they couldn't find is more convincing than pretending. That's the hidden-cost question exactly, and now I know to ask it.

journey.quote: [Costa Navarino](https://www.costanavarino.com/weddings-greece/) in the Peloponnese, [Grecotel Corfu Imperial](https://www.grecotel.com/corfuimperial/weddings-corfu/), [Amanzoe](https://www.aman.com/resorts/amanzoe/celebrations), [Santa Marina](https://www.santa-marina.gr/weddings-celebrations/) on Mykonos and [Katikies](https://www.katikies.com/events/) in Santorini and Mykonos write a proposal on request rather than publishing package inclusions.
journey.reaction: By this point the island run-through is mostly 'no published package' over and over. I skimmed it. Amanzoe and Costa Navarino are the ones I'd actually be curious about, and all I learn is that they don't publish anything.

journey.quote: Its document is direct: "Symbolic weddings /renewal of vows are not legally recognized from the Greek constitution."
journey.reaction: Good, this is the 'confidence the legal side is sorted' bit. Straight from the venue's own document, no hedging. My parents need to read this paragraph.

journey.quote: The registration step sits after the day itself: "The marriage has to be registered by the couple at the Registry Office in Aghios Nikolaos within 40 days after the ceremony."
journey.reaction: 'By the couple' answers whether we have to do it ourselves, at least for that venue. And a Friday wedding means Monday registration, so we can't fly out Saturday. That's the kind of thing I'd have found out too late.

journey.quote: Abaton's brochure gives each named venue its own venue fee, so a fee applies to the space you choose.
journey.reaction: This is the surprise-invoice line. The whole 'What packages often leave out' section is the most useful thing I've read on Greece. Each question is one I'd want to forward to a venue word for word.

journey.quote: In peak season, traffic congestion is severe in the main cities and on the islands, and only licensed taxis with the meter running should be used.
journey.reaction: I came to Transfers wanting to know who gets our grandparents from the airport to the venue. Instead I get a general taxi warning, which is about tourists, not 60 wedding guests. The section never mentions airport transfers at all.

journey.section: Venue package, planner or building your own
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact who plans venue, travel, vendors and payments, anywhere in the world.
journey.reaction: 'Anywhere in the world' is the end-to-end line every planner uses. What I actually want to know is who is standing at the venue on the day when the florist is late. This doesn't say.

journey.section: How to compare two quotes like for like
journey.quote: If one quote answers a point and the other is silent, the silent one is not cheaper. It is unfinished.
journey.reaction: Best line in the piece. The ten questions are going straight into a shared doc with James. This is the bit that makes me think these people know what they're doing.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: There is no agreement between Australia and Greece for free healthcare, so visitors pay for all medical care.
journey.reaction: I would not have thought of that for the grandparents. Mum needs to see this before anyone books flights.

journey.section: For Australian couples: currency, deposits and insurance
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: That's the fourth time I've been told AUD quotes. It's a real plus for us, but saying it in the intro, mid-article, here and at the end starts to feel like a sales line on repeat.

unanswered_questions: Who is physically at the venue on our wedding day: our Wedded Advisor, someone you are accountable for, or the hotel's own coordinator?
Do you arrange airport transfers for guests, including older relatives, or is that left to the venue and us?
Is there a real Greek wedding you've planned, with the venue and date, that I can look at?
For 60 to 90 guests with half flying in from Australia, which of these venues would you actually put on a shortlist?
When you 'plan vendors', do you use your own trusted suppliers in Greece or whoever the venue recommends?

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
turn_offs_found.why: The CTAs themselves are calm, but this same selling point comes back four times (intro, compare-quotes CTA, currency section, closing). Repeated that often it stops reading as a reassurance and starts reading as a script, which makes me wonder how much is template versus a person.

would_share_with: James (partner): the ten-point quote comparison list, so we can send the same questions to every venue
Mum and Dad (contributing): the insurance and healthcare paragraphs and the summer wildfire and heat warning
Both sets of parents: the civil, Orthodox and symbolic section, so they understand what is and isn't legally binding and why we may need to stay past the weekend

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [compare your shortlist with a Wedded Advisor](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=greece-wedding-packages&utm_content=closing), or return to [our curated Greece wedding collection](https://weddedwonderland.com/destinations/europe/greece).
cta_reaction.why: The tone is right and 'compare your quotes' is a genuinely useful offer once we have two. But we don't have quotes yet, and I'd want to see one real Greek wedding you've done and know who's there on the day before handing over our details.

top_3_changes: Make the Transfers section answer the airport question: say which venues mention airport or guest transfers (or that none publish it), and move the general taxi warning lower or cut it.
In the Wedded Concierge 'fourth route' paragraph, say plainly who the couple deals with on the wedding day itself, instead of 'anywhere in the world'.
Say 'quotes in AUD' once or twice, not four times, and trim the 'no published package' run in Island by island so it reads as a quick list rather than a repeated paragraph.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Sophie (planner_couple), using persona voice and concerns
No invented brand facts; missing details listed as unanswered questions
HTML comments and VERIFY markers ignored
Title, business details and absent prices treated as not must-fix; no requests for sourcing lines, per orchestrator

open_questions.question: The Transfers section has no airport or guest-arrival detail. Does the source pack hold any venue's published airport transfer terms the writer could use, or should the section say it is not published?

assumptions: Arrived from a Google search for 'greece wedding packages' during early destination research; no other context was given.
Skimmed the Island by island run and venues capped below 60 guests; read the left-out, legal, quote-comparison and Australian sections closely.
No prices appear by design, so the persona's 'vague pricing' turn-off was not raised.
Family details (grandparents, parents contributing) are persona colour, not brand facts.
The persona card is provisional (not CRM-calibrated).
